subject: RFI: Commercial & Pricing — Commit smoothing and overage mechanism
body_preview: Attached is our commercial appendix with a proposed smoothing mechanism for seasonal bursts; includes commit tiers, true-up cadence, and overage ladder.
messages:
From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acmefinancial.com>, Priya Sharma <priya.sharma@acmefinancial.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Nov 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: RFI: Commercial appendix & smoothing proposal

Hi Jordan / Priya —

Thanks for the RFI. Attached is our commercial appendix that maps the commit tiers, discount ladder, and a proposed smoothing mechanism for seasonality. High-level notes: 

- Commit structure: three-year enterprise commit with annual true-ups (quarterly reporting). Tiers at 100M, 300M, 600M tokens/month average with step discounts between tiers.
- Overage ladder: per-token overage priced at the next lower tier rate with graduated discounts for sustained bursts >30 days.
- Smoothing: we propose a 12-month rolling smoothing bank with 2x burst cushion for seasonal months; quarterly true-ups allow credits to carry forward for a single year.
- Credits & credits bankruptcy protection: unused committed tokens convert to a 6-month credit pool subject to usage patterns; we provide a one-time conversion credit at contract start for migration.

Please see the attached PDF for line-item pricing (on-shore/off-shore instances), examples of billing math, and a worked example for a cyclical usage profile.

Next steps: If the structure looks viable, we can draft the SOW and mark the committed bands you expect to sign to iterate final discounts.

Thanks,
Priya Natarajan
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com | +1 415-555-0127

Attachments: Redwood_Pricing_Appendix_Q4_2026.pdf, estimated-usage-model.xlsx

From: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acmefinancial.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Priya Sharma <priya.sharma@acmefinancial.com>, procurement@acmefinancial.com
Date: Tue, 3 Nov 2026 09:34:00 -0500
Subject: Re: RFI: Commercial appendix & smoothing proposal

Priya —

Thanks for the appendix, it helps a lot. A couple questions from procurement and finance:

1) For the smoothing bank: can you make the carry-forward credits retain the same effective price band? Example: if we purchase at the 300M tier and carry credits forward, will those credits be billed/valued at the 300M discounted rate during a high-burst month?
2) Overage ladder: we need clearer language on how sustained bursts (>30 consecutive days) are identified and whether the overage rate switches automatically or requires manual negotiation.
3) True-up cadence: finance prefers semi-annual true-ups (instead of quarterly) for our internal forecasting. Would Redwood agree?

Also looping in our procurement lead Priya Sharma who will track contract language.

- Jordan
Director, Cloud Platforms | Acme Financial Services
On Tue, Nov 2, 2026 at 3:12 PM Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com> wrote:
> [original message attached]

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 4 Nov 2026 10:08:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: RFI: Commercial appendix & smoothing proposal — internal alignment

Priya / Marissa —

Forwarding Acme's questions. My suggested responses: 

1) Carry-forward credits: yes — suggest we state credits retain the original tier price for a 12-month window (so if purchased at 300M tier, credits apply at the 300M per-token effective price for usage within 12 months). This preserves their unit economics and reduces churn risk.
2) Sustained-burst definition: define as >30 consecutive calendar days with daily rolling average >150% of baseline month average. Automatic re-pricing triggers if sustained burst exceeds 60 days — otherwise we apply elevated overage rate but offer an automatic partial discount if the customer elects to commit to a temporary uplift. Keep manual negotiation as an option for exceptions.
3) True-up cadence: semi-annual true-ups are acceptable if we require a mid-year review checkpoint and allow for an out-of-band true-up if actual cumulative usage variance >30%.

Concession impact: moving to semi-annual true-ups increases credit risk slightly; propose a modest 2.5% reduction in the initial discount ladder to preserve economics unless Acme commits to an increased initial deposit.

If you want, Sean can run the numbers against their example usage model.

-Rishi
Head of Commercial Deals | Redwood Inference

From: Priya Sharma <priya.sharma@acmefinancial.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acmefinancial.com>, procurement@acmefinancial.com
Date: Thu, 5 Nov 2026 11:46:00 -0500
Subject: Re: RFI: Commercial appendix & smoothing proposal

Thanks — that level of detail helps. Quick clarifications: 

- We like credits retaining the tier price for 12 months. Please make the SOW language explicit.
- For sustained-burst automatic re-pricing: we prefer the automatic trigger at 45 days rather than 60, and an explicit 14-day notice window before the higher rate applies so our ops team can respond.
- Semi-annual true-ups are acceptable; can you keep the option for an out-of-band true-up if quarterly forecast deviation >25%?

One additional ask from procurement: can you include a short-term migration credit (one-time) to offset migration costs? We referenced this in the attachment but need it as a line item in the SOW.

If you can update the appendix and SOW with these points, procurement will circulate the contract redline to legal.

Best,
Priya Sharma
Senior Procurement Manager | Acme Financial Services

From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>
To: Priya Sharma <priya.sharma@acmefinancial.com>, Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acmefinancial.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 6 Nov 2026 09:23:00 -0700
Subject: Re: RFI: Commercial appendix & smoothing proposal — updated ask

Hi Priya / Jordan —

Great — appreciate the feedback. Per Rishi's note and your asks, we've done the following changes and attached an updated appendix and SOW draft: 

- Credits: preserved at the original tier effective price for a 12-month rolling window — explicit SOW language added.
- Sustained-burst: automatic trigger set to 45 consecutive days; Redwood will notify Acme 14 days prior to any automatic rate step-up and provide a 14-day remediation window to either accept temporary uplift (automatic for billing at the higher rate) or commit to a temporary uplift purchase to preserve original pricing.
- True-ups: semi-annual cadence accepted; we add an out-of-band true-up clause for forecast deviations >25%.
- Migration credit: added one-time migration credit line in SOW (amount to be agreed; default $50k migration credit reflected as a placeholder).
- Economics: to accommodate semi-annual true-ups without materially impacting unit economics, we offset by moving the base discount ladder back by 1.5% (instead of Rishi's proposed 2.5%). This is reflected in appendix table A-2.

Next steps: If the updated appendix and SOW look good, I propose we schedule an hour to walk legal/procurement through the drafting points (I can join with Rishi and Marissa). Please let us know availability next week and whether the $50k migration credit is acceptable as a placeholder.

Thanks,
Priya Natarajan
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference

Attachments: Redwood_Pricing_Appendix_Q4_2026.pdf (v2), ACME_SOW_draft_v1.docx
